commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a new Format project or document.

commands.name: project
commands.description: Scaffold a new Format project. This works best for a completely empty codebase. For existing codebases, use `format init`.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.description: Where to create the project. Prompted if omitted.

options.description: The framework to build your documents with.
Don't install dependencies after creating the project.
Skip all prompts and use the defaults for every option that isn't provided.

commands.name: document
commands.description: Scaffold a new document directory with an entry file, a stylesheet, and a default data variant.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: The document directory name (kebab-case recommended). Omit it to be prompted with a random suggestion.

options.description: Styling method for the document. Choices are filtered to your project framework. See [/docs/studio/styling](styling docs) for more information.
Scaffold a `data/schema.ts` with this validation library, or "none" for no schema. Format validates any Standard Schema compliant library, so you can also wire up others by hand.
Path to a JSON file to seed the default data variant. Its shape is used to infer the schema and the entry's data type.
Page size for the document. A4 is the default; pass "custom" with --width and --height for an exact size.
Custom page width in CSS pixels. Requires --height; ignored unless --size is "custom" or omitted.
Custom page height in CSS pixels. Requires --width; ignored unless --size is "custom" or omitted.
Don't install missing styling/schema dependencies after creating the document.
Skip all prompts and use the defaults for every option that isn't provided.
Scaffold the most minimal document. Can be combined with other flags.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Set up Format in an existing codebase. This script writes a Format config file, adds npm scripts, gitignore entries, the Format packages, and optionally a first document. Each step will confirm before editing anything.

options.description: The framework to build your documents with — React, Vue or HTML. Detected from your dependencies when omitted.
Where to install the Format project into. The path you give will be set in your Format config's `rootDir`.
Don't automatically add or install any Format packages.
Don't add the npm dev and npm compile scripts to your package.json. Existing dev and compile script names are never overwritten regardless, If there's a name clash, they get a `format:` prefix.
Don't append the `_generated` and `.env` entries to .gitignore. Existing lines are never touched.
Don't offer to create a first document.
Skip all prompts and use the defaults for every option that isn't provided.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds and installs Format packages. Packages will be installed at the version defined in your config file.

arguments.name: packages...
arguments.description: One or more Format packages. Shorthands map to the scope: `zip` means `@format.dev/zip`.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove Format packages from your project. The counterpart to `format add`.

arguments.name: packages...
arguments.description: One or more Format packages. Shorthands map to the scope: `zip` means `@format.dev/zip`.

commands.name: update
commands.description: Move your project to a different Format version. With no arguments, the version set in your Format config file will be used. The argument "latest" updates to the latest available version and pins it.

arguments.name: version
arguments.description: An exact release like `0.1.2`, or `latest` for the newest. Omit it to apply the release already pinned in your config. The version field is the source of truth, and editing it by hand then running `format update` is a supported flow.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the current pinned Format version for your project, check every installed Format package matches it exactly, and mention when a newer version is available. Exits non-zero on any drift, so can be used in CI as a gate.
